subject.title: Memory MVP: build write pipeline with classification, dedupe, merge, and conflict handling

question: Should the Memory MVP write resolver be owned by memory-core as the active-memory write contract, by Memory Wiki as the knowledge-layer workflow, or by a new/expanded plugin API seam before implementation starts?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the request chooses durable memory ownership, schema, provenance semantics, conflict policy, and operator UX that automation should not decide from code alone.

options.title: Design memory-core resolver contract first
options.body: Make memory-core own candidate classification, source-required resolution, canonical create/merge/conflict decisions, and revision history, with Memory Wiki consuming the settled model.

options.title: Route through Memory Wiki
options.body: Treat contradictions, source evidence, and entity normalization as Memory Wiki responsibilities while keeping memory-core as Markdown/search/promotion until a lower-level write API is needed.

options.title: Define a plugin API seam first
options.body: Design a memory write/lifecycle SDK contract so bundled and external memory plugins can implement conservative resolver behavior consistently before choosing the default implementation.

recommendation.title: Design memory-core resolver contract first
recommendation.body: Make memory-core own candidate classification, source-required resolution, canonical create/merge/conflict decisions, and revision history, with Memory Wiki consuming the settled model.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is mostly product and plugin-boundary direction, and this handle has the strongest history on VISION.md and the memory plugin boundary.
